profile.headline: The leading cause of infant bronchiolitis worldwide and a major cause of severe respiratory disease in older adults — and, after sixty years of failure, now preventable at both ends of life.
profile.syndrome: In infants, coryza then bronchiolitis: tachypnoea, wheeze, crackles, feeding difficulty and apnoea in the very young, with the first infection the most severe. Almost everyone is infected by the age of two. In older adults and the immunosuppressed it causes pneumonia and exacerbations of COPD and heart failure, with mortality comparable to influenza. Reinfection throughout life is the rule because immunity is incomplete.
profile.transmission: Large respiratory droplets and contaminated hands and surfaces, on which it survives for hours — hand hygiene matters more than for most respiratory viruses. Highly seasonal in temperate climates, with the pattern disrupted and then restored after the COVID-19 pandemic.
profile.geography: Worldwide, with winter epidemics in temperate regions and rainy-season peaks in the tropics.
profile.diagnosis: RT-PCR on a nasopharyngeal specimen, usually in a multiplex respiratory panel; rapid antigen tests are sensitive enough in infants, whose viral loads are high, but not in adults.
profile.management: Supportive: oxygen, fluids and respiratory support. Bronchodilators, corticosteroids, antibiotics and chest physiotherapy do not help bronchiolitis and all have been shown not to; high-flow nasal oxygen reduces escalation of care. Ribavirin is of marginal benefit and rarely used.
profile.prevention: Nirsevimab, a single-dose long-acting monoclonal antibody, for infants, and palivizumab monthly where nirsevimab is unavailable; maternal immunisation with Abrysvo in pregnancy as the alternative route to the same protection; and Arexvy, Abrysvo or mResvia for older adults. All of them target the prefusion conformation of the F protein, the stabilisation of which is what unlocked the field.
evidence: Isolated in 1956 and causally established by decades of cohort and challenge data; the preventive interventions rest on randomised trials — MELODY for nirsevimab, IMpact-RSV for palivizumab, and the adult vaccine trials. The 1960s formalin-inactivated vaccine, which caused enhanced disease, is the reason the field moved so cautiously for so long.
